page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-optimized cloud server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz across 4 shared virtual cores and 4 physical cores with single-thread allocation. The server includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation suitable for memory-intensive tasks. Hardware storage includes a bundled 200 GB local SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets are supported, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded throughput alongside balanced multi-core execution. The instance scores in the top tier for stress-ng single-core performance (3844.87) as well as single-threaded compression and decompression, achieving 41.08 GB/sec in gzip and 18.68 GB/sec in bzip3. Memory bandwidth reaches 103.01 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 47.08 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core compute and general utility metrics remain consistent across synthetic suites, registering 5500.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 12.13 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads.

Without dedicated GPU hardware, the instance exhibits weak performance in larger machine learning inference tasks, such as 7B parameter language models. However, its 8:1 memory-to-CPU ratio and fast single-thread execution offer solid cost efficiency for memory-heavy, non-GPU applications. Workloads that match this profile include in-memory databases, Redis caches, CI/CD compilation pipelines, text and image processing services, and mid-sized transactional databases requiring substantial RAM relative to compute capacity.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 shared AMD EPYC 9575F vCPUs at 2.0 GHz, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 200 GB local SSD on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with support for AVX-512 vector and cryptographic instruction sets, it delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier single-core compute and compression efficiency, evidenced by strong stress-ng single-core scores and 41.08 GB/sec gzip compression throughput. Multi-core operations, memory bandwidth, and web serving speeds sit in the average performance tier. With zero dedicated GPUs, large neural model inference is constrained, making the instance less practical for heavy AI workloads. It offers efficient resource allocation for data-heavy configurations such as in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, web application hosting, and software compilation tasks requiring substantial memory per execution thread.
